crosswalks.label: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers
crosswalks.rationale: O*NET directly describes software QA analysts/testers and its task structure substantially overlaps the package's reproduction, regression, test-design and defect-evidence work.

crosswalks.label: Software and applications developers and analysts not elsewhere classified
crosswalks.rationale: ESCO/ISCO places software testing and quality-assurance occupations within a broader software-analysis/development unit, so the relation is useful for hierarchy but not an exact profession boundary.

findings.summary: Public occupational evidence strongly supports defect identification, reproduction, regression/negative/usability testing, test plans/scripts/procedures and recording test results.
method_labels: O*NET occupation task and detailed-work-activity evidence
findings.rationale: The existing body already has exact-state intake, reproduction, regression design, boundary/state probing, evidence classification and release-evidence procedures.

findings.summary: O*NET QA work includes documenting defects, bug tracking/reporting and maintaining known-defect information, making defect lifecycle/state a recurring professional structure rather than a one-off report.
findings.rationale: The body emits reproduction reports and handoffs but lacks a first-class defect/known-failure lifecycle contract with identifiers, duplicate/supersession state and owner routing.

findings.summary: Occupational evidence includes using and maintaining testing software plus test environments/tools as part of QA work, not only executing individual fixtures.
findings.rationale: The current tools are executor-neutral runners/observers, but the body does not yet reconstruct test-tool/environment configuration, maintenance, calibration or fitness-for-purpose deeply.

findings.summary: QA occupational evidence includes participating in design reviews and providing input on functional requirements, schedules and problems, while not owning those product/design decisions.
findings.rationale: The body correctly avoids feature/product authority but could make early design/review consultation an explicit handoff rather than appearing mostly post-implementation.

gaps_against_body.description: Add a defect/known-failure lifecycle contract covering stable identifiers, reproduction evidence, duplicate relationships, status/supersession and explicit owning-profession handoff without granting QA product authority.
Research and reconstruct test environment/tool configuration, maintenance, calibration/fitness and environment drift as professional machinery separate from product failure evidence.
Add an explicit early design/requirements review consultation route where QA supplies testability/risk evidence without deciding product scope or design intent.

nonclaims: This packet does not establish complete QA coverage for enterprise systems, mobile, distributed systems, load/performance, accessibility, security, regulated validation or every software domain.
An O*NET occupation profile describes common occupational work; it does not prove every QA specialist performs every listed task.
The existing Ghost Studio TEST evidence remains bounded to its recorded game/software scope and is not widened by this research packet.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: No authorization, regulated validation, security acceptance, or product decision authority is created by this research packet.
